Date of Notice: 2026-08-21
Requested Service: Lower back disc surgery/decompression, CPT 63030
Ordering/Treating Provider: Reyes, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the Anthem Appeals Review Team:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 63030 (laminotomy/hemilaminectomy with decompression of nerve root(s), single interspace, lumbar), communicated in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-21. The stated reason for denial was that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." I am submitting this appeal within the 180-day window stated in the notice (by 2027-02-17) and am requesting that Anthem reverse this determination based on the clinical documentation summarized below.

I understand that this request was reviewed against the clinical criteria applied by Carelon Medical Benefits Management (the vendor Anthem uses for musculoskeletal/spine-surgery prior authorization review) in its "Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines — Musculoskeletal Appropriate Use Criteria: Spine Surgery," section "Lumbar Discectomy, Foraminotomy, and Laminotomy," effective 11/15/2025. I want to be transparent about the scope of what I am able to quote directly: the only guideline language below appears in quotation marks because it was retrieved verbatim from that document. Where I describe the substance of a criterion without quotation marks, that is my own paraphrase, and I am formally requesting that Anthem/Carelon provide me and Dr. Reyes with the complete, verbatim text of every specific criterion applied to this denial, including the full bulleted list of qualifying findings under the "Radicular pain (radiculitis/radiculopathy)" indication, so that we can respond to each element precisely.

1. The denial reason concerns imaging correlation, and the record demonstrates that correlation.

The guideline's general framework states that "the results of all imaging studies should correlate with the clinical findings in support of the requested procedure," and that "if discrepancies should arise in the interpretation of the imaging, the radiologist report will supersede." The imaging and clinical findings in this case are directly correlated, not discordant:

- MRI of the lumbar spine performed 2026-06-09 documents an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root.
- The patient's radicular pain radiates into the right calf — a distribution consistent with L5 nerve root involvement at the L4-L5 level shown on imaging.
- Physical examination documents positive provocative testing on the affected (right) side and a neurologic deficit "corresponding to the imaged level," per the exam note in the prior authorization packet.

This is a single-level, side- and level-matched correlation between the imaging abnormality (L4-L5 extrusion, right lateral recess stenosis, traversing L5 root compression) and the clinical presentation (right-sided provocative signs, right L5-distribution radicular pain, and a neurologic deficit at that level). I am asking Anthem to identify, specifically, what additional correlation the reviewer found lacking, since the imaging report, the exam findings, and the reported symptom distribution all reference the same side and the same nerve root.

2. The guideline's general clinical framework elements are met.

The guideline's General Clinical Guideline section states that before any intervention, "it is essential that the clinician confirm the diagnosis or establish its pretest likelihood based on a complete evaluation of the patient. This includes a history and physical examination and, where applicable, a review of relevant laboratory studies, diagnostic testing, and response to prior therapeutic intervention." That evaluation is documented here: a 14-month history of progressive low back pain unrelieved by rest, a completed course of conservative therapy, medication trial, an interventional injection, and diagnostic MRI confirming a structural cause (L4-L5 extrusion with lateral recess stenosis and nerve root compression) that matches the exam and symptom pattern.

The guideline also states that appropriateness depends on whether "the anticipated benefit of the recommended intervention is likely to outweigh any potential harms" and whether "there exists a reasonable likelihood that the intervention will change management and/or lead to an improved outcome for the patient." Given the failure of a complete, well-documented conservative program to relieve the patient's pain and functional limitation, and the presence of an imaging-confirmed, side- and level-matched structural lesion, surgical decompression is reasonably likely to change management and improve the patient's function, consistent with this standard.

3. Conservative management has been exhausted.

The record documents the following conservative treatment, all prior to the imaging and surgical request:

- 12 weeks of supervised physical therapy (core stabilization and lumbar flexibility), 20 visits completed, 2026-04-04 through 2026-06-27, with a documented discharge note.
- 8 months of NSAID therapy with inadequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-03, which produced only 2 weeks of partial relief.
- A total symptom duration of 14 months, with the pain unrelieved by rest.

I have not been able to independently confirm the exact wording or duration threshold the "Lumbar Discectomy, Foraminotomy, and Laminotomy" section requires for conservative care, and I am not quoting or asserting specific policy language on that point because I have not been able to obtain it verbatim. I am asking Anthem/Carelon to state plainly, in writing, whatever specific conservative-care duration or modality requirement was applied in this denial, so that this extensive and well-documented conservative-care history (14 months of symptoms, 12 weeks/20 visits of supervised PT, 8 months of NSAIDs, and an injection) can be evaluated against it directly.

4. Functional impairment supports the request.

The patient is unable to stand for more than 10 minutes at a time and has ongoing radicular pain into the right calf. This is the kind of "significant functional impairment" referenced in the guideline's discussion of radicular pain with correlating physical exam findings, although — again — I do not have the complete verbatim bullet list under that heading and am not quoting language I cannot confirm.

Additional relevant facts: there is no active infection, no untreated substance use, the patient's BMI is 29, and the patient is a non-smoker — none of which present any contraindication to surgery.

Requested Action

Based on the above, I am requesting that Anthem:
1. Reverse the denial and authorize CPT 63030 as requested by Dr. Reyes.
2. If the denial is not fully reversed on this record, provide the complete, verbatim clinical criteria that were applied — including the specific bulleted findings required under the "Radicular pain (radiculitis/radiculopathy)" indication and any conservative-care duration requirement in the Lumbar Discectomy, Foraminotomy, and Laminotomy section — so that any remaining gap can be addressed directly.
3. Offer a peer-to-peer conversation between Dr. Reyes and the reviewing physician, consistent with the guideline's own statement that "the determination of appropriateness will most likely require a peer-to-peer conversation to understand the individual and unique facts that would justify a finding of clinical appropriateness" when initial elements are not otherwise established to the reviewer's satisfaction.
